body:
Source: the ADLC principle-fidelity audit (delta.md, PR #486). Split out of seam 7 during build.

The suppression-marker scan (packages/rails-guard/lib/suppressions.mjs, findSuppressions)
matches via case-sensitive scanText.includes(marker) over a closed list. The audit flagged
this as dodgeable by case/whitespace/unicode. BUILDING seam 7 surfaced that the obvious fix
— blanket case/whitespace/unicode normalization — is WRONG and would DEGRADE the gate:

- .skip( / .only( (JS), @ts-ignore / @ts-expect-error (TS), eslint-disable (ESLint), xfail
  (pytest), #[ignore] (Rust) are all CASE-SENSITIVE in their own tools. A mangled/upper-cased
  or homoglyph variant is INERT — it dodges the scanner but also fails to suppress anything.
  Normalizing them would false-positive on non-functional lookalikes and block legitimate code.
- The one genuinely OPERATIVE dodge is # noqa: flake8 honors #noqa, # NOQA, #NOQA, #  noqa
  (case- and space-insensitive). The current 'includes("# noqa")' misses those operative forms.

So the correct fix is OPERATIVE-AWARE and per-marker, not blanket normalization — the
operative-vs-inert-authoritative lens the doctrine already prescribes for text-scanning gates.

CROSS-MODEL GATED at P5 (touches packages/rails-guard, an enforcement/trust-root package):
a same-model clean prosecute is not enough; needs a cross-model-review approve.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOR
1. Match # noqa case-insensitively and with optional interior whitespace (regex /#\s*noqa/i),
   covering flake8's honored forms, without touching the case-sensitive markers.
2. Do NOT case/unicode-normalize the case-sensitive markers; adding false positives on inert
   lookalikes is the bug. If a marker has documented operative variants in its tool, match
   those specifically; otherwise keep the exact-substring match.
3. Preserve the hardened diff parser and the doc/MDX inert-span handling unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An added line with #noqa (no space) or '# NOQA' (caps) is flagged as a suppression. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/suppressions-operative.test.mjs`
- An added line with an INERT case variant of a case-sensitive marker (e.g. .SKIP( or @TS-IGNORE) is NOT flagged (no false positive). verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/suppressions-operative.test.mjs`
- Existing suppression tests still pass unchanged. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/suppressions.test.mjs`

allow-suppression: none
title: rails-guard: catch operative suppression-marker dodges (not blanket normalization)
